new.n: James Murphy's missing ~$24,000, Murphy farm barnyard, Warsaw Twp (Rice Co.)
new.pl: Murphy farmstead on the sec. 23/24 line, T109N R21W (Warsaw township), Rice County (1915 Webb atlas)
new.v: About $24,000 in gold coin (1902 value), unfound
new.st: Early settler James Murphy kept "large amounts hidden about the house" and died suddenly about 1902 without telling where. His widow had once counted the hoard at about $30,000. In April 1920 a cow's hoof broke through a rotten board in the barnyard of son Frank Murphy's farm, and grandson Sylvester found an old crock with $6,000 in gold, at a spot once "just outside the barnyard" and later taken into the lot. The family felt "more akin to disappointment than elation": roughly $24,000 was still missing. The 1915 Webb atlas shows the Murphy farm in the west part of sec. 24 with building dots on the sec. 23/24 line, the farmstead and its barnyard.
new.t: About four-fifths of a counted hoard never found, on a farm that can be placed. Check the old barnyard and house site on the 1938 aerial. Private land: ask permission first.
src: Faribault Daily News via People's Press (Owatonna), 14 May 1920, p. 2 (newspapers.com 1025567305)
